summary: Targeted verification of Telehealth ad-hoc room randomization + light regression. Ad-hoc rooms are now cryptographic UUIDs (vpp-<uuid v4>) — verified two consecutive Start Session clicks produced DIFFERENT random rooms; end-call returns to list. All 5 role logins still succeed. Backend regression: 52/53 pytest passed; the 1 failure is a test-hygiene issue (residual login_attempts lockout for the shared XFF from prior iteration), not a code regression — backend/server.py was unchanged this round.

minor.issue: test_brute_force_lockout_returns_429 fails on first attempt with 429 because a prior run left an active lockout row for XFF 10.99.88.77. Test should clear db.login_attempts for that key in a fixture, or use a fresh random XFF per run.

telehealth_verification.per_appointment_ui_note: Seed DB currently has 0 active appointments for doctor/receptionist, so tele-join-<id> buttons did not render. Code path start(`vpp-${a.id}`, ...) is unchanged and was verified in iteration_4. Backend appointments endpoint is healthy (pytest OK).

action_items: (Low priority) Make test_brute_force_lockout_returns_429 self-cleaning: delete db.login_attempts row for the XFF/email key at test setup, OR generate a fresh random XFF per run.
critical_code_review_comments: randomRoomId() correctly prefers window.crypto.randomUUID() with a getRandomValues fallback — good. Minor: the fallback branch does not throw if neither API exists (returns an all-zero id) — acceptable given all supported browsers implement getRandomValues, but a hard error would be safer if a legacy browser ever hit it.

Room name is passed via URL query params (?room=vpp-<uuid>&name=...). The random UUID is unguessable, but note it is still visible in the browser address bar / referer headers if a user opens external links from the page. Consider using history.replaceState with a scrubbed URL once the call is active, if referer leakage is a concern for the threat model.
Prior review items still stand: server.py is 570+ lines (split into routers); consider TTL index on login_attempts.updated_at for auto-expiry (this would also fix the flaky brute-force test).
seed_data_creation: None new. Prior TEST_ prefixed data cleaned by existing pytest teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Telehealth ad-hoc security fix VERIFIED — window.crypto.randomUUID() produces vpp-<uuid v4> rooms, distinct per click, jitsi container mounts, end-call returns to list. Per-appointment path (tele-join-<id>) not UI-tested this iteration because the seed DB has no active appointments; if you need to test it, first create one appointment via reception then click tele-join-<id> and assert the URL room param equals vpp-<appt uuid>. Brute-force test is flaky across iterations due to shared XFF lockout state; either add a cleanup fixture or use random XFF.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature works. Only flake is test hygiene (login_attempts collection not cleared between iterations).
